episodes.title: Engineering and Reverse-Engineering Intelligence Using Probabilistic Programs, Program Induction, and Deep Learning

screening.publisher_promise: NIPS 2017 tutorial by Josh Tenenbaum and Vikash Mansinghka on probabilistic programs, inference programming and program induction.
screening.screening_reason: The originators of the probabilistic-programming account of intelligence: common sense as inference in structured generative programs (intuitive physics and psychology as game-engine-like models). It is the strongest competing account to purely statistical learning in modules 4 and 6, and the repo has no Tenenbaum. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (scaling critique from deep learning) · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: Which inferences need structured programs rather than amortized networks, and what do they gain in sample efficiency and generalization?
screening.caveat: Video hosted on the NeurIPS Facebook page; date and length not shown on the venue page.

episodes.title: Tom Griffiths | CMBC Lecture: The Rational Use of Cognitive Resources

screening.publisher_promise: Emory Center for Mind, Brain and Culture lecture on resource-rational models of cognition.
screening.screening_reason: Griffiths and Lieder’s resource rationality: replace unbounded optimality with optimal use of limited computation, so apparent biases become rational trade-offs. A unifying principle for reasoning under compute limits, relevant to module 5 and test-time compute. Rubric: A originator ✓ · B unifying principle ✓ · C derivation ✓ · D 2 (unfalsifiability critique in BBS commentaries) · E 2 · F 2.
screening.transcript_question: How is the cost of computation formalized, and what does the framework predict that an unbounded Bayesian model does not?
screening.caveat: Title and channel verified by YouTube oEmbed; the event page gives about 74 minutes (2023), not independently verified.
